name: 试卷与知识图谱
description: The paper/knowledge engine: the 24 routes of api/papers, api/paper-submissions, api/knowledge, api/wrong-questions and api/study-plans, lifted out of api/modules/learning after plugins/assignments took the Prisma-free assignments+exams half (P4.3b.5b). Adopts the 16 tables of its own schema cluster - papers and their assets/sections/items/answers/submissions/rubric points, the question bank, the knowledge graph, wrong questions and their attempts, study plans and their items. Reaches students only through `classroom.public`, so the ownership check in ctx.db is the proof that it never touches another domain's table.

services.name: learning.public
services._note: The question bank, the knowledge graph and the wrong-question book, for a plugin that needs to reason about a student's learning. First consumer: `plugins/ai-study`, whose engine picks practice questions and writes mastery back. This port exists because guardrail G1 forbids a plugin reading another plugin's tables, and `data.reads` would not have been enough - the write (`recordPracticeOutcome`) has to run under this plugin's ownership, since mastery is one number with one definition and the student's 错题本 is where it is shown. Deliberately answer-free in the outward direction: neither the question refs nor the signals carry `answer_json` or `explanation`, because judging an answer is the owner's job and a student-facing API built on this port therefore cannot leak an answer key by accident. Refusals are return values, matching `ClassroomResult`: `getStudentSignals` answers `null` for a student that does not exist. Authorization is *not* here - a port has no request actor, so a consumer proves the student is its own to ask about through `classroom.public` first, which is the same split `PetAuthorization` records. Hard dependency, not optionalPeers, for consumers: there is no personalisation to compute without a bank.

data._adopted_note: These 16 tables are exactly the ones the migrated code reads or writes - measured, not guessed: `grep 'prisma\.(papers|paper_|questions|rubric_points|subjects|knowledge_|question_knowledge|wrong_question|study_plan)' api/modules/learning/learning.service.ts` before deletion, plus the JOIN-free child lookups the repository performs. They keep their legacy names because `SELECT *` rows are the HTTP contract and renaming them is the coordinated P7 namespace migration (guardrail G10). Child tables stay with their parents, because neither has meaning alone and the delete paths (`savePaperStructure` -> `deletePaperStructure`) remove children first explicitly - `rubric_points.paper_item_id` does declare `ON DELETE CASCADE` (`api/schema/legacyBootSchema.ts`), but `rubric_point_scores` references both `paper_answers` and `rubric_points` with no cascade, so the explicit child-first order is what the cleanup rule preserves as well. (This sentence claimed the opposite until P4.3b.14 checked it against the DDL.) `question_knowledge` is the questions<->knowledge_nodes join table, read by `generateWrongQuestionPractice`. P4.3b.14 added `notes` and `rubric_point_scores` for a different reason - see `_ownership_note` - which makes 18. Still NOT adopted, deliberately: `knowledge_products`, `note_assets`, `note_products` sit in the same schema cluster but no route in this plugin touches them; claiming them would inflate the G10 ratchet for tables this domain does not serve.
data._ownership_note: P4.3b.14 added two tables that had NO owner at all, so that they could have a cleanup rule for account deletion (a rule may only name tables its plugin declared): `notes` and `rubric_point_scores`. The boot schema creates both and only the old admin cascade ever touched them, through Prisma, which bypasses the ownership check - so nothing had ever needed to answer who owns them. They are learning's because they are this plugin's schema cluster: `rubric_point_scores.answer_id -> paper_answers.id` and `rubric_point_scores.rubric_point_id -> rubric_points.id` are foreign keys into tables this plugin already owns, and `notes` carries the teacher/student/class triple whose papers and study plans this plugin deletes. This is the same shape as classroom's P4.3b.14 adoption of five orphan tables and identity's P4.3b.7 adoption of `users`/`activation_codes`/`activation_events`: giving an existing, previously unowned table its first owner, not claiming someone else's.
data._reads_note: Empty on purpose, and that is the design: this domain needs `students` (the caller's own student row) and nothing else from outside its own tables, and `students` is classroom-owned, so it is fetched through `ctx.use('classroom.public').getStudentByUserId(actor.userId)` instead. Declaring `students` here would both weaken the ownership model (a read declaration where a port exists) and invite a direct query. Every statement in `learning.repository.ts` therefore names an adopted table, and the non-production ownership check in `ctx.db` enforces it on every call.
data._auth_note: All 24 routes are actor-guarded as of the route-authorization round (`docs/security/route-authorization-matrix.md`, the learning table). Twenty-one already were - the controllers call `requireActorRole` before delegating. The three knowledge-graph reads (`GET /api/knowledge/subjects`, `GET /api/knowledge/nodes`, `GET /api/knowledge/edges`) were this domain's last `无鉴权` rows and now carry the same gate, at the matrix's 应属角色 登录用户（teacher/student/admin）: a login gate, not a scope filter, because the graph is course content and carries no user data - and `parent`, which that column does not list, is refused with 403 as it is nowhere in this domain. `GET /api/papers` and `GET /api/papers/:id` are deliberately unchanged: they hand `actorOf(req)` to the service, which is the authority on what a teacher (their own papers) or a student (their own class, published only) may read - a read filter, not a second gate. The split is 401 `未登录或登录已过期` for an unknown caller, 403 `无权限执行该操作` for a known one who may not, and it always fires before any validation message. Nothing on this surface remains open; `node scripts/security/route-authorization-audit.mjs` reports `learning 24 0 24 0`.
data._known_debt: 1. `api/modules/admin` still deletes from eight of these tables during `DELETE /api/admin/users/:id` (`admin.repository.ts:242-369`: papers, questions, paper_items, rubric_points, paper_submissions, paper_answers, wrong_questions, study_plans) through Prisma `$transaction`, which bypasses `DbApi` entirely - so the ownership check cannot see it. Same debt as plugins/assignments and plugins/pet; it must become a port call (or disappear with admin) when that domain migrates. P4.3b.14 discharged it: the cascade's eight deletes are now this plugin's own cleanup rule (`src/learning.cleanup.ts`, registered in `setup()`), which the runtime runs in the same transaction as every other plugin's rule, so the account-deletion path no longer writes these tables through Prisma at all. The other half of the note stands: `api/modules/insights` does NOT read these tables (verified by exhaustive grep), unlike the assignments half. 2. `POST /api/papers/:id/assets` writes a file into `<cwd>/uploads/papers` with `node:fs`, as the deleted service did. A `restricted` plugin has no declared filesystem capability for this; the honest fix is a host-provided storage port, which does not exist yet. 3. Missing-row `update`/`delete` still answers **500** (the Prisma P2025 status the legacy translator produced for an unknown id) rather than 404 - preserved on purpose; the 500 body now carries the kernel envelope's message instead of the driver's. A measured example: `DELETE /api/knowledge/nodes/2` with a dependent row used to answer a raw Prisma P2003 dump (absolute paths and source lines included) and now answers `{success:false,message:"服务器内部错误"}` - same 500, less leaked. 4. The route `base` entries above are the real controller prefixes (`/api/papers`, …), which the manifest validator warns are not namespaced under `/api/learning`; that warning is expected - these are the paths the deployed frontend calls, and the legacy names are the contract. 5. FLOAT STORAGE DRIFT, measured by the P4.3b.6b equivalence probe: `POST /api/wrong-questions/:id/attempt` computes `Math.min(1, Math.max(0, mastery + 0.2))` identically in both revisions, but the *stored double* differs. Prisma's engine bound the value through its own path and landed on the double nearest 0.3; better-sqlite3 binds the raw IEEE-754 double, so `0.1 + 0.2` is stored as 0.30000000000000004 (`quote()` = 3.000000000000000445e-01). Invisible in HTTP: `JSON.stringify(0.1 + 0.2)` is `0.3`, so no response body changed. The value only differs when read at full precision straight out of SQLite. `knowledge_edges.weight` has the same exposure for non-representable inputs. Decide at P7: a rounding step in the repository, or accept the raw double.
